clue.text: Honour a new monarchy

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A newly founded kingdom is honoured.
explanation.definitionFit: Oman is a Gulf sultanate, a state ruled by a hereditary monarch, so it is an example of a monarchy.

clue.text: Again fix limits concerning US agent being put up in Spain

parts.note: re means concerning or about

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting a word up writes it from bottom to top, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a Fed is an FBI agent in American slang
E is the international vehicle registration letter for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: Someone redraws a boundary after an American agent is lodged in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: To redefine is to set out the bounds or meaning of something anew, fixing its limits a second time.

clue.text: Engineers tax break

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
a cess is a tax or levy

explanation.surface: A tax holiday granted to engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: A recess is a pause in work or sitting, such as a parliamentary holiday: a synonym for a break.

clue.text: Season with popular ground termite

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters of the word termite are reshaped

explanation.surface: A seasonal pest: the termite, popular and grinding away.
explanation.definitionFit: Wintertime is the winter period, one of the four seasons of the year.

clue.text: Ceremony before Queen not right in World Heritage Site

indicators.note: before places the ceremony word ahead of the next piece

parts.note: pomp is ceremonial display

indicators.note: not right says to drop R, the abbreviation for right, from the royal title

parts.note: ER II, Elizabeth Regina the Second, stands for the late Queen

explanation.surface: A royal ceremony held at a famous historic site, with the Queen not quite right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not right' removes R from ERII, the Queen's cipher, leaving EII.
explanation.definitionFit: The ruined Roman city near Naples is on UNESCO's list, so it is an example of a World Heritage Site.

clue.text: Asian dish made by the Italian in French town

indicators.note: in places the Italian article inside the name of the French town

parts.note: Pau is a town in south-west France
il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: An Italian makes an Asian dish in a French town.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilau is spiced rice cooked in stock, a dish of South Asian and Middle Eastern cooking.

clue.text: Nowise mention broadcast when recreation is due

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, as seed is, so the letters of the two words are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A broadcaster is told not to mention anything until the break.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in your own time means doing it in your free hours, the leisure period when recreation is allowed.

clue.text: Send away former wife to French island

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse
île is French for island

explanation.surface: Packing off an ex-wife to an island off France.
explanation.definitionFit: To exile someone is to banish them from their country, a synonym for sending away.

clue.text: Soft bottom part of peer with honour

parts.note: an earl is a peer of the realm
OBE, Officer of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

explanation.surface: A decorated nobleman has a soft bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: The fleshy lobe hanging at the base of the outer ear is its soft lowest part.

clue.text: Start of preparation to train horse to dive

indicators.note: start of picks out the opening letter of the word preparation

parts.note: to lunge a horse is to exercise it on a long rein in a circle

explanation.surface: Preparing a horse for a jump starts with schooling it to dive.
explanation.definitionFit: To plunge is to throw oneself headlong into water, a synonym for dive.

clue.text: Capsize open vessel

parts.note: overt means open, not hidden
an urn is a vessel such as a vase or tea urn

explanation.surface: An open boat is liable to capsize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a boat, fitting 'Capsize', but here it is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: To overturn is to turn something upside down, as a boat does when it capsizes.

clue.text: Cars have a sort of merit in start/stop devices

indicators.note: have means hold within, so the cars word holds the other piece

parts.note: autos are motor cars

indicators.note: a sort of suggests a variant version of the word merit, its letters reshuffled

explanation.surface: Cars are praised for their start/stop technology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start/stop' reads like stop-start motoring, fitting the cars, but the devices are timers in general.
explanation.definitionFit: Autotimers switch appliances on and off automatically, so they are devices that start and stop things.

clue.text: Frequently of XX

parts.note: read X as the Roman numeral ten followed by X as the multiplication sign, giving ten times

explanation.surface: Twenty times, it happens frequently.
explanation.walkthrough: XX looks like the numeral twenty, but the first X is ten and the second is the 'times' sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Oftentimes is an old-fashioned word meaning often, on many occasions.

clue.text: Cross as marsupial died

parts.note: roo is short for kangaroo, a marsupial
D is the abbreviation for died in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone is angry because their kangaroo has died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' reads as angry, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A rood is a crucifix, especially the large one above a church's chancel screen.

clue.text: Delayed after big bang?

parts.note: the phrase means arriving late, and it is also literally true of anything after the Big Bang, which started the clock of the universe

explanation.surface: Something postponed after an explosion.
explanation.walkthrough: Everything after the Big Bang happened literally once the universe's clock was running.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means 'and about time too', used of something overdue or late.

clue.text: Running in to bat it's all or nothing

indicators.note: running suggests the letters of in to bat move about and settle in a new order

explanation.surface: A batsman going out to the crease knows it's all or nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Not a bit means not at all, none whatsoever, so it amounts to nothing.

clue.text: Convert reviled grasping old sinner

indicators.note: grasping means holding inside, so the rearranged letters wrap round the next piece
convert means change into another form, so the letters of the word reviled are rearranged

explanation.surface: A religious convert, once reviled, clutches an old sinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convert' rearranges REVILED to EVILDER, and 'grasping' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An evildoer is a wrongdoer, someone who does wicked things: a synonym for a sinner.

clue.text: Stagger forward — going back would be mad

indicators.note: going back means the word for mad is read backwards, while forward the letters give the answer

parts.note: nuts is slang for mad

explanation.surface: A drunk staggers forward; trying to walk backwards would be madness.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to astonish or shock, the sense in which news can stagger someone.

clue.text: The enemy seen in middle distance

indicators.note: seen in means appearing inside, so the enemy word sits within the middle word

parts.note: the centre is the middle
time is the enemy, a stock phrase (time is the great enemy)

explanation.surface: The enemy is spotted at middle distance.
explanation.walkthrough: TIME is 'the enemy' from the saying that time is the enemy of us all.
explanation.definitionFit: A centimetre is a hundredth of a metre, a unit for measuring length or distance.

clue.text: Pure tea's initially taken with Ecstasy

parts.note: cha is tea, and the 's is kept, giving cha's

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of the word taken

parts.note: E is the drug Ecstasy

explanation.surface: Pure tea is first taken alongside a drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means sexually virtuous or plain and unadorned, both senses of pure.

clue.text: Cultivate endless strawberries in France

indicators.note: endless means both outer letters are cut off the French word

parts.note: fraises is French for strawberries

explanation.surface: A French gardener cultivates strawberries.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise crops or animals is to grow or breed them, a synonym for cultivate.

clue.text: They have independent importance and got off with alibi

indicators.note: off means wrong or amiss, so the letters of got and alibi are disordered

explanation.surface: A criminal got off thanks to an alibi.
explanation.walkthrough: This variant spelling of obbligati, plural of obligato, comes from music, where the term marks an instrumental part.
explanation.definitionFit: Obligati are musical parts that are essential and independent, not to be left out of a performance.

clue.text: Four up and four more to play in large bedroom, that is

definitions.text: Four up and four more to play

parts.note: a dorm, short for dormitory, is a large shared bedroom
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A golf match in a dormitory.
explanation.walkthrough: In match-play golf, dormie describes a player as many holes ahead as there are left to play.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer four holes ahead with four still to play cannot lose, the exact situation called dormie.

clue.text: Get reward from scripture teaching before meals

parts.note: RE is religious education, the school subject
a.p., ante prandium, is the Latin prescription abbreviation for before meals

explanation.surface: A child gets a reward for listening to Bible study before lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: A.P. (ante prandium) appears on prescriptions to mean take before meals.
explanation.definitionFit: To reap is to gather in the harvest, and figuratively to obtain the reward of one's efforts.

clue.text: The measure for crime

parts.note: ft is the abbreviation for foot or feet, a measure of length

explanation.surface: Crime has a measure that should be taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Theft is the act of stealing, one particular crime.

clue.text: French and going round following the Spanish girl, 18

indicators.note: following places the reversed French word after the Spanish article and the girl

parts.note: el is the Spanish masculine article the
Eva is a girl's name

indicators.note: going round means turned about, so the French conjunction is read backwards

parts.note: et is French for and

explanation.surface: French and Spanish girls going round together.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 refers to the answer to 18 down, RAISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To elevate something is to lift it higher, a synonym for raise.
